QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_24

question.text: Per the SEBI ICDR Regulations 2018 (Chapter X-A), 'Social Enterprise' means:

answer.text: Only a Not for Profit Organisation that meets the eligibility criteria.
Only a For Profit Social Enterprise that meets the eligibility criteria.
Either a Not for Profit Organisation or a For Profit Social Enterprise that meets the eligibility criteria under the SEBI ICDR Regulations.
Any entity registered under the Companies Act 2013 with at least one CSR activity.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook p.60, a 'Social Enterprise' means either a Not for Profit Organisation or a For Profit Social Enterprise that meets the eligibility criteria specified under the SEBI ICDR Regulations. The definition is inclusive of both legal families but gated by the eligibility criteria. The Trap: Options A and B each capture only half of the inclusive definition. Option D collapses 'Social Enterprise' into 'any company doing CSR', which misses the eligibility tests entirely. Note: The eligibility tests apply equally whether the entity is an NPO or an FPE — the definition is form-agnostic.
